name: C-Quest Capital

summary.text: C-Quest Capital (CQC Impact Investors LLC) is a Washington-area developer of carbon-credit projects, including clean-cookstove programmes registered with the Verra registry. In October 2024 the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York unsealed fraud charges against its founder and former chief executive Kenneth Newcombe and a former executive, Tridip Goswami, over inflated emissions-reduction data; prosecutors declined to charge the company itself, citing its self-disclosure and cooperation. The same day the SEC entered a settled cease-and-desist order against C-Quest over a $250 million offering, and the CFTC said CQC had settled and agreed to pay a $1 million civil penalty.

CFTC Charges Former CEO of Carbon Credit Project Developer with Fraud Involving Voluntary Carbon Credits

facts.claim: On October 2, 2024 the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York unsealed charges against C-Quest Capital's former CEO Kenneth Newcombe and former executive Tridip Goswami over a scheme that, prosecutors alleged, led the company to obtain carbon credits worth tens of millions of dollars by fraud.
facts.quote: in connection with a scheme to commit fraud in the carbon markets, which resulted in their company, CQC Impact Investors LLC ("CQC"), fraudulently obtaining carbon credits worth tens of millions of dollars

sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
sources.title: U.S. Attorney Announces Criminal Charges In Multi-Year Fraud Scheme In The Market For Carbon Credits

facts.claim: Prosecutors said they would not bring criminal charges against the company itself, citing its voluntary self-disclosure, cooperation and remediation.
facts.quote: Prosecutors decided not to bring criminal charges against CQC itself, citing its voluntary self-disclosure, cooperation, and remediation.

sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
sources.title: U.S. Attorney Announces Criminal Charges In Multi-Year Fraud Scheme In The Market For Carbon Credits

facts.claim: The SEC's settled order found that former senior C-Quest personnel orchestrated a scheme to manipulate and inflate the carbon credits generated by and estimated from the company's projects, in connection with a $250 million offering; C-Quest consented to a cease-and-desist order without admitting or denying the findings.
facts.quote: former senior C-Quest personnel had orchestrated a scheme to manipulate and falsely inflate the amount of carbon credits generated by and estimated from C-Quest's projects

sources.title: Order Instituting Cease-and-Desist Proceedings, Securities Act Release No. 33-11315

facts.claim: The CFTC said CQC settled the agency's allegations and agreed to pay a $1 million civil monetary penalty.
facts.quote: CQC settled with the CFTC and agreed to pay a $1 million civil monetary penalty.

sources.title: CFTC Charges Former CEO of Carbon Credit Project Developer with Fraud Involving Voluntary Carbon Credits

facts.claim: Reporting said that in June 2024 C-Quest disclosed it had found wrongdoing that led to over-issuance of credits from its Verra-registered cookstove programmes, and that Verra suspended 27 implicated projects pending review.
facts.quote: In June 2024, C-Quest said it had found wrongdoing that led to over-issuance of credits tied to its Verra-registered cookstove programs, and Verra suspended 27 implicated projects pending review.
